_doc: THE EFFORT ROUTING TABLE: every subagent launch carries the effort its ROLE maps to here.
Owner decision 2026-10-12. The brief's FIRST non-empty line is `ROLE: <role>`; the launch's
per-dispatch effort parameter (Claude Agent/Task `effort`, Codex spawn_agent `reasoning_effort`,
normalized to `effort` by lib/codex-hook-runtime.js::normalizeNativeInput) MUST equal the level
this table assigns to that role. hooks/dispatch-contract-guard.js enforces it at PreToolUse and
BLOCKS on a missing or malformed role line, an unknown role, a missing effort, a different effort,
or a `fork` launch (which runs at its parent's effort) that carries no override line; the
next non-empty line `EFFORT-OVERRIDE: <level> — <reason>` permits a different level and is
recorded in the override use ledger. Measured basis: the per-dispatch parameter IS honoured on
both runtimes (Claude low x3 87-88k tokens / 2 tool calls vs high x3 95-208k / 5-8; Codex
reasoning tokens low 18-42 vs high 326-661).
SCHEMA, checked by lib/effort-routing.js::validateRoutingTable — and FAIL-CLOSED: any violation
makes the table INVALID, and an invalid (or absent, or unparseable) table blocks EVERY launch
with a `routing table invalid` reason. There is no built-in default table to fall back to.
- top-level keys: exactly `schema_version` (the integer 1), `roles`, and optional `_doc`
(an array of strings); any other key is INVALID
- `roles`: a non-empty object; each key a lowercase kebab-case role name, each value one of
low | medium | high | xhigh | max
Consumers: the dispatch-contract guard now; the Decision engine's dispatch-plan later
(workspaces/context-budget-2026-10-10/engines/ENGINES.md § 2). Change a level HERE, never in
either consumer.
